## Fonts, licences and replacements

The owner's four questions, answered from the records below (rebuilt on every run, never typed). A replacement counts as found when its face is bundled in the pinned opf-render manifest. Licensed (proprietary) fonts are never bundled or embedded; the PPTX keeps the selected name.

| Question | Count | Breakdown |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| How many fonts do we have? | 168 | 71 open, 97 proprietary |
| How many are licensed so we can use them directly (open)? | 71 | 67 drawn as themselves, 4 open aliases (Liberation Mono, Liberation Sans, Liberation Serif, Source Sans Pro) |
| How many need a replacement (proprietary)? | 97 | 53 proprietary-latin, 41 proprietary-script, 3 special |
| How many have a replacement found? | 97 | 9 metric-compatible, 44 visual look-alike (Latin), 41 script face, 3 special path (3 code-table) |
| How many have no route? | 0 | none |

Licence of the bundled faces: the 97 replacement routes use 50 distinct faces, by licence OFL-1.1 (50); the pinned opf-render manifest holds 66 packages and 197 faces (packages: OFL-1.1 (66); faces: OFL-1.1 (197)). The open families themselves: OFL-1.1 (71). Only OFL-1.1, Apache-2.0, MIT and UFL-1.0 may be bundled ([font-licensing.md](font-licensing.md#font-files-bundling-and-licenses)).

A route found is not a route verified: 168 families are native verified, 0 partial and 0 failed (see Native evidence); the special path is described under Symbol-encoded families.

This is the per-font work list behind the owner's 2026-09-29 review. Each record holds the family's selected name, preview route and tier, the bundled face (package, version, hashes, styles), the styles it needs and lacks, scripts, per-style measurements, host and native verification, parity signals, phase, status, next action and evidence. A family counts as accepted (status qualified or documented-visual) only when its own fixtures pass in every host and, for a proprietary family, its measurement against the real font is on record (RR-17); every other family still needs its own fixture and acceptance record, Native PowerPoint verification is recorded only where a committed native run (see Native evidence) names the family; every other family is unverified.

## Summary

168 records: 168 policy families. 168 route to a face that opf-render bundles (a code-table route counts when every face of its chain is bundled); 0 do not. 7 records were read by the committed parity run in a way that is stale against main (rerun needed).

| Status | Count | Severity | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `loading-gap` | 0 | 3 | The family's preview face is not bundled by opf-render, so every host falls back to another face. A face that is bundled but not yet released to one host (the gallery editor) is noted in hostLoading and the next action, not counted as a gap. |
| `style-gap` | 0 | 2.5 | The preview face is bundled, but styles the family needs are missing from the bundle. |
| `policy-gap` | 0 | 2 | A face ships in the renderer but the family has no row in the font policy registry. |
| `needs-special-path` | 0 | 3 | No ordinary look-alike can serve the family and no code-table route is bundled for it: it needs a dedicated math, emoji or symbol-encoding path. |
| `code-table` | 3 | 1.5 | A symbol-encoded family (Symbol, Wingdings, Webdings) previews through a code table (FF-45, opf-render#94 and #95): each code maps to Unicode and draws with the first loaded open Noto symbol face at the verified font's advance. The route is bundled and verified in opf-render's node, browser and raster tests; native PowerPoint verification of symbol runs is not recorded, and the open glyphs differ in shape from the originals. |
| `visual-gap` | 2 | 2 | A bundled visual look-alike is routed, with styles present; metric qualification, appearance or measurement work remains. |
| `script-gap` | 41 | 2 | A bundled Noto script face is routed. The script corpus (FF-44) qualifies its coverage and shaping and measures the installed original where there is one; no open face is metric-compatible, so the route stays visual, and the native PowerPoint comparison (FF-46) and any recorded appearance gap (compact originals, serif originals) remain. |
| `baseline-needed` | 38 | 1 | An open family is bundled with the styles it needs; a fresh per-host verification and acceptance record is the remaining work. |
| `metric-measured` | 0 | 0.5 | A metric-tier route measured against the real font in four styles on the source path (width bar met). Vertical metrics and line breaks are not yet recorded, and per-host and native verification remain, so it is not verified. |
| `documented-visual` | 43 | 0.5 | RR-17: a bundled visual look-alike with its own fixture in every host (node, browser, editor, gallery editor) and its measured gaps against the real font recorded (widths per style, line breaks, vertical metrics, outlines, coverage). Reflow against the real font is expected and documented; native PowerPoint verification (FF-46) remains. |
| `qualified` | 41 | 0.1 | RR-17: an open family that draws as itself, or a metric route whose four-style widths and line breaks are within the bar, with its own fixture in every host (node, browser, editor, gallery editor). Native PowerPoint verification (FF-46) remains. |

| Phase | Count | Owner's phase |

| 1 | 38 | Reconcile and baseline |
| 2 | 0 | Loading and style coverage |
| 3 | 0 | Aptos compatibility |
| 4 | 46 | Remaining replacements |

| Host | Verified | Unverified | NA |

`verified` means per-family evidence exists in a repository; `unverified` means a face is routed but no per-family acceptance exists; `NA` means no intended face exists to load in that host. Hosts: `node` (opf-render registries; the default `prepareNodeFonts` pack is `base`, Roboto only, and the office, open and script packs load only when requested), `browser` (opf-render browser registry), `editor` (the opf-editor playground), `galleryEditor` (the vendored opf-editor bundle inside pptx.gallery, 33 eager faces) and `galleryCards` (pptx.gallery's self-hosted preview webfonts for cards and pages, upright regular and bold only). Loading routes per host are in each record's `hostLoading`.

## Priority queue

Priority: score = severity x (valuesOpen x hostFactor + 1). severity is the status severity, plus 0.5 for a visual Latin route whose measured maximum width delta exceeds 5%. valuesOpen counts parity values whose preview uses the family and whose fontResolution is not already pass (real face or metric replacement with the selected name kept). hostFactor is the share of applicable hosts without per-family verification, never below 0.25. The audited set is 850 gallery values (parity-results-2026-10-01-published-0.11.9-gallery-d8f5ae6.json).

| 1 | Arabic Typesetting | proprietary-script | 4 | `script-gap` | 4 | 8.4 | Native PowerPoint comparison (FF-46, RR-05) is the remaining acceptance gate. Script corpus 2026-10-01: Noto Naskh Arabic (400, 700) has complete own-script coverage and its measured advances equal HarfBuzz's on 24 of 24 face-samples; the same samples agree in Chromium within 0.1 px. Installed original read in place: width delta +56.0% mean, 74.5% max over 12 samples; line height 1.15 (original) against 1.7 em (preview face). No open face of the script is this narrow, so the row carries `sizeAdjust` 0.64 (RR-38): the preview scales the replacement's size by it in measurement and drawing, so lines have PowerPoint's length (the unadjusted preview drew 56 percent longer lines). ## Script corpus (FF-44)

Result of the script shaping corpora ([script-corpora.md](script-corpora.md)): each family's preview face run through the corpus samples of its script (coverage, fontkit against HarfBuzz, browser), and, for a proprietary family whose original is installed on the measuring host, the original read in place. A width delta is the replacement's advance over the original's, minus one, on the corpus samples of the family's script; line height is hhea ascent plus descent plus line gap in em. Not a native PowerPoint claim.

## Native evidence

Native PowerPoint checks are supervisor-run (root owns Office); only their committed comparison output counts here. Basis: Native name read-back: supervisor-run PowerPoint 365 read the family's selected name from every run (latin, East Asian, complex script) and from the theme slots of a saved deck that names it, and the names matched the export. It does not accept the preview face's look or metrics against the real font (image scores are reported, not gated). 168 families are verified, 0 partial and 0 failed (a deck that reads the family back fails a gated check: fonts, themeSlots or presentationFonts); a family no run names stays unverified.

## Symbol-encoded families (FF-45)

Symbol, Wingdings and Webdings are not text fonts: their glyphs sit at codes 0x20 to 0xFF of a Microsoft Symbol cmap. opf-render previews them through a code table (opf-render#94 and #95; [special-families.md](special-families.md)): each code maps to Unicode through core's [symbol-font-encodings.json](../../../spec/reference/symbol-font-encodings.json) and draws with the first loaded open face of the chain (pinned at opf-render `8f0d6f1`), at the verified font's advance. The route kind is `code-table` and the status `code-table`: the route exists and is verified in opf-render's node, browser and raster tests. Native PowerPoint verification of symbol runs is not recorded for any of them. Wingdings 2 and Wingdings 3 share the Wingdings policy row and have no record of their own.

| Family | Chain (first loaded face draws) | Codes mapped | Bundled | Node / browser | Native |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Symbol | Noto Sans, Noto Sans Math, Noto Sans Symbols 2, Noto Sans Symbols | 189 of 224 codes | yes | verified / verified | verified |
| Webdings | Noto Sans Symbols 2, Noto Sans Symbols, Noto Sans Math, Noto Sans | 223 of 224 codes | yes | verified / verified | verified |
| Wingdings | Noto Sans Symbols 2, Noto Sans Symbols, Noto Sans Math, Noto Sans | 222 of 224 codes | yes | verified / verified | verified |

## The owner's plan

Owner input, 2026-09-29, adopted as the program order. Request: "work this in as a tracker and to help prioritize work."

> The owner completed 160 font-specific reviews: all 153 policy registry families plus seven shipped script-font dependencies missing from the registry. No repository files were changed by those reviews.
>
> 1. Reconcile the inventory and establish a fresh baseline. Record each font's selected name, preview face, version, hashes, available styles, scripts, and acceptance evidence.
> 2. Finish loading and style coverage. Connect the shipped editor, gallery, browser, and Node hosts to the intended faces; eliminate unintended fallbacks.
> 3. Prioritize Aptos and Aptos Display compatibility. Measure them separately and qualify candidates before adopting them.
> 4. Complete the remaining replacement work. Packaging, script shaping, and metric compatibility remain separate deliverables.
> 5. Complete native verification and rerun the full parity audit. Keep source, installed-package, and live-site claims separate.
>
> Aptos and Aptos Display are the critical path: each appears in 704 of the 850 audited gallery values.

Rules:

- Every family gets its own fixture and acceptance record. Grouped rows share work, but a result for one family does not establish acceptance for another.
- For proprietary fonts, PPTX always retains the user's selected name.
- Preview replacements must use pinned, permitted files.
- Metric qualification requires per-style measurements, matching line breaks and line metrics, and the unchanged geometry tolerances, not just a favorable average width.
- The current Latin-only corpus must also be extended with script-specific text.
- Most script packs currently provide regular and bold only. Required italic or other styles need genuine qualified faces; diagnostics preserve honesty but do not complete an outstanding fidelity requirement.

## Reconciled with current state

The owner's review predates some merged and in-flight work. The records above use current truth: core `origin/main` policy and docs, the pinned opf-render manifest, and the latest committed parity run. What changed against the review:

- Aptos family (the owner's review predates this). Intos, Intos Display, Intos Narrow and Intos Serif measured 0.000% mean and maximum width delta in all four styles against Aptos 2.01, with equal vertical metrics and original (Inter-derived; serif Gelasio-derived) outlines under OFL-1.1 with no Reserved Font Name. They are the metric routes in policy (opf#166), vendored in opf-render (#54, `d528be5`, pinned commit `fef9315c`) and loaded lazily by browser hosts (opf-editor#42). Independently re-verified for Aptos, Aptos Display and Aptos Narrow; Aptos Serif was measured from Microsoft's Aptos Fonts download. The parity run on the merged mains passes all 704 Aptos and Aptos Display values, so they no longer lead the priority queue. Node and browser verification is recorded for the family; the editor playground test covers the Aptos scheme (Aptos and Aptos Display); the gallery editor waits for a release. The owner's "no verified compatible replacement" is superseded.
- The committed parity run (opf#175 first, on the merged mains opf `338ddcd4` and opf-render `d528be5`: 660 perfect, 33 near and 157 mismatch, with fontResolution 733 pass, 31 near and 86 fail) is now the 2026-09-30 run on the published engines with the gallery editor font host modelled: 729 perfect, 108 near and 13 mismatch over 850 values, with fontResolution 755 pass, 92 near and 3 fail. Earlier runs are history.
- Georgia now has a metric tier: Gelasio with liga and clig disabled (opf#163, opf-render#49, including the raster ZWNJ fix). The parity run on the merged mains reports it as a metric substitute for all 6 values.
- Open families are now vendored from unmodified upstream or npm packages (opf-render#50): Open Sans, Montserrat (including 900), Poppins, Bebas Neue, PT Serif, Lora, Merriweather Sans, Source Sans 3 (with the Source Sans Pro alias), Red Hat Display (300, 400, 700) and Red Hat Text (400, 700). Raleway and Playfair Display are not bundled because resvg ignores the wght axis. The owner's "bundle" rows for the bundled families become verification work; FF-43 then bundled Anton, Archivo Narrow, Barlow, Bitter, EB Garamond, Figtree, Libre Caslon Text and Work Sans and completed Red Hat (see the FF-43 note below). The remaining bundling work is Liberation Mono, Sans and Serif, Playfair Display and Raleway.
- Carlito is vendored as unmodified google/fonts files (opf-render#58) because its Reserved Font Name applies. Licenses, Reserved Font Names and no-hotlink rules are guarded in core and the renderer (opf#165, opf-render#53).
- Script fonts: previews load script faces when the `scripts` option is passed (opf-render#55, opf-editor#40) and fall back per character to Noto Sans (opf-render#57). The parity run of 2026-09-30 models the gallery editor host (its font gate loads the script and vendored faces a document needs), so the 88 family uses it used to record as `missing` now resolve to their Noto route; loading is not verification per family. Still failing there: Raleway and Playfair Display (not bundled; the editor draws Roboto) and the Noto Sans Mongolian face, which cannot shape any text.
- Hosts are recorded separately. The default Node registry (`prepareNodeFonts`) uses the `base` pack (Roboto and Roboto Mono only); the office-pack faces (Carlito, Arimo, Tinos, Cousine, Gelasio, Caladea, Intos) and the open pack load only when `pack: 'office'` is requested, and script faces only when the `scripts` option is passed. Browser hosts and the opf-editor playground load the 33 eager base and office faces and now load the vendored open pack and Intos lazily, on demand (opf-render#54, opf-editor#42). The gallery editor (a vendored opf-editor bundle) gets them only with a release that includes opf-editor#42, so it is recorded as pending, not as a gap in the family's status.
- Gallery cards are a different host from the gallery editor. pptx-gallery self-hosts preview webfonts (pptx-gallery#53 and #54; replacement data in #51) as upright regular and bold faces from pinned @fontsource packages, unmodified upstream files or the vendored Intos faces. The tracker reads that list from a pinned snapshot (`galleryCards`, refreshed 2026-10-02 at pptx-gallery 5af1c5f: 51 families, 138 faces). Card previews do not change the editor's bundle. A family's card host is `verified` when pptx-gallery's tests/preview-fonts.test.ts covers it (a font scheme uses it, its stack resolves to the hash-pinned licensed face, weights and glyph coverage hold, no recorded coverage gap); a family no font scheme uses, or whose card face has a recorded coverage gap, stays `unverified`. The snapshot was pinned at efb63ac (2026-09-29) and had not been refreshed since, so it counted no card family as verified.
- fontResolution treats a policy look-alike as near, not fail, when the PPTX names the selected family (opf#159). Parity harness fixes merged in opf#164 and opf#168. The value set is 850 after pptx-gallery#40 removed 50 unsupported chart types; Aptos and Aptos Display each appear in 704 of them.
- Selawik 1.01 was measured and rejected as a Segoe UI replacement (opf#166: regular 0.16% mean and 2.51% max on the standard 300-string corpus, 0.73% and 9.7% on the reviewer's broader corpus); Red Hat Display stays the visual route. Segoe UI Light, Semilight and Semibold were measured separately.
- Cover slide centering (opf-pptx#97) is geometry work with no font impact.
- The seven shipped script-font dependencies that were once missing from the registry (Noto Sans Arabic, Sinhala, Lao, Myanmar, Thaana, Syriac and Noto Serif Tibetan) have policy rows since RR-17 (FF-44), so no record is a policy-gap and `extras` is empty.
- FF-43 (open replacement faces, opf-render branch claude/ff-43-bundle-open-candidates with this companion change): Barlow and Anton (google/fonts statics, byte-identical at commit 23e54b51ddff), Figtree, Work Sans, EB Garamond, Archivo Narrow, Libre Caslon Text and Bitter (npm-derived @expo-google-fonts statics, exact versions; no Reserved Font Name except Bitter, whose reserved name "Bitter Pro" is in no face name) are bundled with only the styles the policy needs, lazy in browser hosts; the eager list stays 33 faces. Red Hat Display now ships 300, 400, 600 and 700 with italics and Red Hat Text 400 and 700 with italics: the RedHatFont repository statics were unusable (the Regular, Light and SemiBold italics (and Red Hat Text Italic) do not set the OS/2 italic bit (only the Bold Italic files do), Red Hat Display SemiBold declares weight 707 and Bold 799 (Red Hat Text Bold declares 700), so a 600 request paints as Bold and the regular and bold italics as one face in resvg, probed), and Red Hat has no Reserved Font Name, so the correctly labelled @expo-google-fonts instances replace them. Libre Caslon Text has no bold italic upstream (explicit gap). The 19 rows whose route face was measured are re-measured (Rockwell on Bitter: 1.1% to 4.4% mean, up to 8.5% max) on 2026-09-29 against the installed Windows originals; the widths are unchanged (except Corbel and Gill Sans MT, which now follow the vendored Source Sans 3) and every row stays visual: none meets the metric bar. Grandview, Grandview Display, Tenorite and Tenorite Display are not installed on the measuring host and stay unmeasured. Trade-off: the shipped Red Hat Display Bold is about 2.5% narrower than the RedHatFont Bold it replaces (Segoe UI Bold preview mean width +0.6% to -1.8%, mean absolute 0.95% to 1.86%).
- RR-17 follow-up (2026-10-02): the tracker answers the owner's four questions in `summary.licensing` (how many fonts, how many open, how many need a replacement, how many have one, and the licence of the bundled faces). Symbol, Wingdings and Webdings now carry the code-table route that opf-render#94 (FF-45) added: previewRoute kind `code-table` through the chain pinned in font-tracker.symbol-fonts.json, status `code-table`, node and browser verified, native unverified. Native PowerPoint evidence is read from the committed comparison output of the RR-05 runs (`overrides.nativeEvidence`): a family is native verified only when a deck that names it passes per-run fonts, theme slots and Presentation.Fonts. The style rule now takes a proprietary family's declared styles as the real font's (Cambria Math and Segoe UI Emoji ship one face, so their four-style requirement was an assumption, not a gap).
- FF-46 (2026-10-02): the supervisor ran 43 decks (225 slides, every family named by at least one deck) in PowerPoint 365 on the 0.12.0 train (opf 0.12.0, opf-render 0.12.0, opf-pptx main with FF-05) and the comparison output is committed in docs/evidence/ff-46-native-0.12-20261002: every deck passes per-run fonts, theme slots and Presentation.Fonts (no extra and no missing names), so all 168 families are native name verified. That is a name read-back only: the check says nothing about the look or metrics of the preview face against the real font, and a family that is not installed on the host is still read by its selected name. A deck has one theme, so only the first family of a multi-family deck is read through its own theme slot; every family is read through per-run names and Presentation.Fonts.
- FF-46 follow-up (2026-10-02): native verification has a `failed` status. A family that a deck reads back (theme slot or Presentation.Fonts) or names, where that deck fails a gated check (fonts, themeSlots or presentationFonts; a deck that did not open fails fonts) and no passing deck reads it back, is `failed`: `nativeVerification.failures` lists the run, deck, failing checks and mismatch kinds, the next action says to triage it, and `summary.nativeFailedFamilies` lists the families. A passing deck that reads the family back keeps it `verified` with the failing deck as a caveat. The committed FF-46 run has no failed family.

Inputs: policy version 1 (168 families); opf-render manifest at `8f0d6f1bbdec82f266494113e7e061b931bf44e2` (66 packages, 197 faces, captured 2026-10-02); measurement report corpus 300 Latin strings; parity run 2026-10-01T14:39:22.606Z at opf `e414bca`, opf-render `2fbc0ab`, opf-pptx `a9bcbd7`, pptx-gallery `d8f5ae6`.

## Records by phase and class

Columns: Route is the preview face and tier (main's policy; an in-flight route is noted). Bundled lists the styles opf-render ships for the route face and what it lacks. Width delta is mean and maximum |ratio - 1| of shaped advances against the real font on a Latin corpus (per-style values are in the JSON); script families have no script-specific corpus yet. Values counts parity values that use the family.

Installed original read in place: width delta +56.0% mean, 74.5% max over 12 samples; line height 1.15 (original) against 1.7 em (preview face). Native name read-back passed (ff-46-native-0.12-20261002), so any step above that only confirms the selected name is done; acceptance of the drawn look and metrics against PowerPoint remains. | [Font licensing and policy table](font-licensing.md), [Special families: symbol-encoded fonts](https://github.com/OpenPresentation/opf/blob/main/docs/programs/font-fidelity-everywhere/special-families.md), [opf-render test/symbol-fonts.mjs and test/symbol-fonts-browser.mjs](https://github.com/OpenPresentation/opf-render/blob/main/test/symbol-fonts.mjs), [opf-render#94](https://github.com/OpenPresentation/opf-render/pull/94), [opf-render#95](https://github.com/OpenPresentation/opf-render/pull/95), [FF-46 native run: every family on the 0.12.0 train](../../evidence/ff-46-native-0.12-20261002/README.md) |

## Method

- **Selected name.** The PPTX always retains the selected family. The parity typefaces and fontResolution checks read the exported names back for the audited values; the record's `paritySignals.pptxNamedValues` counts them.
- **Route and tier.** From `spec/reference/font-policy.json`, resolving provisional decisions. `metric` needs a mean below 0.1% and a maximum of at most 0.3% in all four styles; `visual` is a documented look-alike. Width deltas alone do not qualify a face: matching line breaks and line metrics, vertical metrics and unchanged geometry tolerances are also required and are unrecorded (`verticalMetricsMatch`, `lineBreaksMatch` are null) except for the in-flight Intos candidate.
- **Bundled.** From the pinned opf-render manifest snapshot: package, version or commit, license, Reserved Font Names, file names and SHA-256 per face. For a proprietary family it describes the route face, never the proprietary font.
- **Styles.** Style keys are weight plus `i` for italic (`400`, `700i`). Required styles come from the measurement report where the real font was on the measuring host, otherwise four styles for Latin and regular and bold for script families are assumed (`stylesBasis`). An open replacement must also carry the styles of every family routed to it (`stylesRequiredByRole`).
- **Parity signals.** From the committed run named above, which models the gallery editor font host (its font gate loads the script and vendored faces a document needs). `statusAtRun` is what the run observed; `expectedStatusOnMain` is what current main should produce; `rerunNeeded` marks a mismatch.
- **Evidence.** Merged and in-flight pull requests, evidence folders and docs. In-flight work is labelled and never counted as merged.
